idiom_name: actor-confined state (Akka/Pekko) or single-threaded ExecutionContext; DynamicVariable for dynamic scope
implementation_notes: On the JVM, `ThreadLocal`/`InheritableThreadLocal` are available from Java and Scala's stdlib wraps the latter as `scala.util.DynamicVariable`, which binds a value for the dynamic extent of `withValue` and gives every new thread a copy of the current binding stack. But the idiomatic Scala answer to confinement is to not call the object from arbitrary threads at all: keep mutable state inside one actor (Akka/Pekko) and express every interaction as a message - the actor runtime guarantees one-message-at-a-time processing and publishes the required happens-before edges, so plain `var` fields need no volatile or locks. A single-threaded `ExecutionContext`/dispatcher achieves the same for plain Futures. The classic ThreadLocal form stays justified for thread-affine interop - JNI handles, per-worker JDBC connections, MDC logging context.
pitfalls: Actor confinement holds only while state stays inside: closing over actor state in a Future callback or sending a mutable reference as a message reintroduces races (use pipeToSelf/context.ask for completions).
DynamicVariable copies bindings at thread creation, but thread pools create threads once - values set by one task are stale or invisible in the next task on the same pool thread.
ThreadLocal and Future/ExecutionContext continuations do not compose by default: the continuation may run on any pool thread, so values silently reset between callbacks.
